title: The date-range control offers the standard presets plus Custom and does not offer "All Time" — expected, do not file
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. The Inventory Value report is open.
steps: 1. Open the date-range control in the toolbar.
2. Read every option offered.
expected: 1. The control offers the standard presets: "Today", "Yesterday", "This Week", "Last Week", "This Month", "Last Month", "This Year", "Last Year", "This Quarter", "Last Quarter", and "Custom".
2. "All Time" is NOT offered — because the report is valued as of a single date, an All-Time option would be meaningless; its absence is the documented v1 behavior.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
notes: DOCUMENTED LIMITATION — DO NOT FILE. The missing "All Time" option is a deliberate v1 boundary.

title: The report values inventory as of the END of the selected range — the date is an as-of anchor, not a created-date filter
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Nightly snapshots exist for past dates at the selected location (recording has been running).
3. A part exists that was ALREADY in stock before the selected range started.
steps: 1. Select a past range (for example "Last Month").
2. Check which date the displayed values represent.
3. Look for the part that was stocked before the range started.
expected: 1. The report values inventory as of the END of the selected range.

2. The date control is an "as of" anchor, not a created-date filter — narrowing it does not select "parts added in that range"; it shows the whole shelf as it stood on that date, so the part stocked before the range still appears.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)

title: When the selected window reaches today and today has not been recorded yet, the report values the current live stock
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Today's nightly snapshot has not yet been recorded (the normal daytime state).
3. A ZZAUTOTEST part's on-hand quantity was changed TODAY (after last night's capture).
steps: 1. Select a range that reaches today (for example "This Month" or "Today").
2. Find the part whose quantity changed today and read its row.
expected: 1. The report values the current live stock — the values represent today.
2. The part's row reflects today's changed quantity (not yesterday's snapshot), proving the live fallback is in use.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
spec_ref: specs/inventory-value.md Story 5 S5-R3; §3 Key Decisions (live fallback for today)

title: For a past date the report replays the closest recorded day on or before the end of the selected range
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. Nightly snapshots exist for past dates, and a ZZAUTOTEST part's quantity is known to have DIFFERED on a past recorded day from its quantity today.
steps: 1. Select a Custom range ending on the past recorded day.
2. Find the part and read its quantity and values.
3. Compare them to what the part held on that recorded day (not today).
expected: 1. The report replays the closest recorded day on or before the end of the selected range.
2. The part's row shows the quantity and values recorded for that day, not today's live stock.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
spec_ref: specs/inventory-value.md Story 5 S5-R4; §2 Relationship to nightly history

title: An "As of" indicator names the day actually shown when it is earlier than the date asked for, and is hidden when they match
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. A past date exists that has NO snapshot of its own but has an earlier recorded day before it (for example, a gap day, or a date in the thinned monthly-retention band).
steps: 1. Select a Custom range ending on the gap date (a date with no snapshot of its own).
2. Look for an "As of" indicator and read which day it names.
3. Then select a range ending on a day that IS recorded (or today with live values) and look for the indicator again.
expected: 1. When the displayed day is an earlier recorded day than the date asked for, the report shows an "As of" indicator naming the day actually shown.
2. When the displayed day matches the date asked for (the common current-view case), the "As of" indicator is not shown — the date control already communicates the date.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
notes: VIU-confirm the indicator's exact on-screen wording — the spec pins "As of " plus the day but not the full label format.

title: A Custom range lets the user pick start and end dates, values as of the picked end date, is capped at today, and reloads on change
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. The Inventory Value report is open.
steps: 1. Open the date-range control and choose "Custom".
2. Pick a start and an end date in the past and apply.
3. Try to pick an end date in the future.
4. Watch the data area when the range is applied.
expected: 1. A Custom range lets the user pick a start and end date, and the report values as of the picked end date.
2. A future end date cannot be chosen — the end date is capped at today.
3. Changing the date range reloads the report (the loading indicator shows and the rows re-fetch).
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
notes: VIU-confirm how the today-cap is enforced (disabled future dates vs an error).

title: History accrues forward only — a date before the first nightly recording cannot be reconstructed — expected, do not file
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. The date nightly recording began at this organization is known.
steps: 1. Select a range ending before the first nightly recording.
2. Read what the report shows.
expected: 1. The report shows the empty state — there is no way to reconstruct inventory value for a date before recording began, because there is no historical backfill.
2. This forward-capture-only behavior is the documented v1 boundary, not a defect.

spec_ref: specs/inventory-value.md Story 5 S5-E1; §2 Known Limitations (v1); §2 Out of scope
notes: DOCUMENTED LIMITATION — DO NOT FILE. Forward-capture history only; no backfill exists.

title: The Category and Vendor filters are multi-selects that reload the report to only the matching parts
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. In-stock parts exist across at least two categories and two vendors.
steps: 1. Open the filter labeled "Category" and select one category; watch the data area.
2. Add a second category to the selection.
3. Clear the Category filter, open the filter labeled "Vendor", and select one vendor; then add a second.
expected: 1. The toolbar has a Category filter labeled "Category" and a Vendor filter labeled "Vendor", each allowing one or more selections.
2. Selecting one or more categories reloads the report to show only parts in the selected categories.
3. Selecting one or more vendors reloads the report to show only parts supplied by the selected vendors.

title: Category, Vendor and part search are server-side; each change returns page 1
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. The unfiltered result set spans multiple pages, and matching parts for a category/vendor/search exist BEYOND page 1.
steps: 1. From page 2 (or later), select a Category and check which page shows and which rows are listed.
2. Repeat with a Vendor selection.
3. Repeat with a part search.
4. Also change the date range, the location selection, and the sort — watching the data area each time.
expected: 1. Each change re-queries the server and returns the first page of the new result set.
2. The filtering covers the ENTIRE data set — matching parts that were on later pages appear — not just a narrowing of the rows on the current page.

3. Every change — date range, location, Category, Vendor, part search, sort — reloads the rows from the server; while loading the standard reports loading indicator shows, and existing rows are replaced only when the new data returns.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
spec_ref: specs/inventory-value.md Story 6 S6-R5; Story 1 S1-R4; S1-R5; S1-R7; S1-R8

title: The part search is a page-local toolbar field matching part number OR description, case-insensitively, on the server
permissions_required: A role with the existing inventory-reports permission (Story 1 prerequisite).
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser.
2. In-stock parts exist whose part numbers and descriptions you know (including a description containing a distinctive word).
steps: 1. Find the part search input in the report's own toolbar (not the application's global search bar).
2. Type part of a part number and read the results.
3. Clear it and type part of a description, in a DIFFERENT letter case than the stored text.
4. Type text matching nothing.
expected: 1. The search field is page-local, in the report's own toolbar — it is not the application's global search bar (the same toolbar-search pattern used elsewhere in the reports suite).
2. The report narrows to parts whose part number OR description contains the entered text.
3. Matching is case-insensitive.
4. The search applies server-side (whole data set, first page returned); a no-match search shows the no-data message.
design_ref: none — design not yet available (spec-only authoring)
notes: Parts Velocity is the spec's named sibling for this same search pattern. VIU-confirm the search field's placeholder/label text (unpinned).

2. Read its position in the toolbar and its default selection.

title: Scoping never includes an inaccessible location, and a selection resolving to none falls back to the user's active location
permissions_required: A user with access to some, but not all, locations, and the inventory-reports permission.
preconditions: 1. You are signed in to the ShopView App on a desktop browser as a user who can access some, but not all, of the organization's locations.
2. The Inventory Value report is open.
steps: 1. Open the Location filter and read the locations offered.
2. Use "Clear all" so the selection resolves to no location, and watch what the report loads.
expected: 1. Only the locations the user has access to are offered — a location the user cannot access is never included in the scope.
2. If the requested location set resolves to none the user can access, the report falls back to the user's currently active location.
